newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks drop again despite portfolio buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks drop again despite portfolio buying.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.27 percent on Monday despite some limited portfolio buying to bolster prices ahead of end-of-year "window dressing" book-keeping, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped for a fourth consecutive trading day to 151.56 points in quiet business worth just 530,819 dinars ($749,744).

"Portfolios that are carrying stock at high cost are trying to activate trade to prop up end of year trading to reduce losses in end-of-year window dressing," said one broker, pessimistic of a market rebound in the remaining week before the New Year.
Two stocks that dominated trade on Sunday, National Industries, expected to benefit from the oil-for-food deal, and heavyweight stock Arab Bank were again the heaviest traded shares on Monday.
National Industries rose 0.02 dinars to 0.77 in turnover of 76,956 dinars. Arab Bank slipped 0.50 dinars to 250.50 dinars after shares worth 110,390 changed hands.
The third heaviest traded stock, International Tobacco, expected to announce strong 1996 profit, shed 0.01 dinars to 1.01 dinars in turnover of around 67,200 dinars.
But falling shares outnumbered gainers by 24 to 13, with another nine trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.50 percent to 82.50 points from 82.92 points, still 13.62 percent down from the start of the year.
